name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
summary: Faye emphasizes national sovereignty, social protection, domestic industrial development and African cooperation. His current record combines institutional reform commitments with conservative positions on same-sex relations and continued negotiations with international lenders.

universal-healthcare.rationale: He expands universal health-insurance enrollment and connects family assistance with public insurance coverage.

unions-good.rationale: He praises constructive union engagement and makes sustained social dialogue essential to national transformation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He demands employers comply with labor rights, social obligations and fair taxation.

cut-welfare.rationale: He strengthens family security grants and adaptive social protection rather than cutting these programs.

strong-leader.rationale: His reform project seeks stronger constitutional restraints on presidential power rather than unchecked executive concentration.

state-harmful.rationale: He seeks stronger public labor administration and social-protection institutions.

empower-police-military.rationale: He supports new security units, military modernization and expanded police and gendarmerie deployment.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He says legalization of same-sex marriage abroad shocked him, while respecting other states’ legislative sovereignty.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He wants education rooted in Senegalese languages, traditions, culture and values.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He advocates revitalized multilateral institutions and reform that gives Africa a stronger role in global decisions.

free-trade.rationale: He criticizes global protectionist fragmentation while supporting continental free-trade arrangements; his position is qualified.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He supports operational regional and continental peace forces alongside UN missions with clear mandates.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He advocates coordinated industrial development, domestic resource processing and a continental defense industry.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He institutionalizes tripartite consultation through the national social-stability pact and labor-law negotiations.

democracy-best.rationale: He praises democratic alternation and institutional resilience as national strengths.

political-violence-never.rationale: No stated position on political violence; support for regional military responses to security threats is something nearby.

collective-farming.rationale: Supports family farms alongside voluntary cooperatives.

positive-liberty.rationale: He ties inclusion to practical access to insurance, employment and financing for disabled people.

force-without-un.rationale: He condemns unilateral force contrary to the UN Charter and prefers multilateral action.

class-collaboration.rationale: He advocates reciprocal responsibilities and durable cooperation among government, employers and workers.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He advocates expansive public welfare, labor regulation and economic support beyond defense and property protection.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He describes voters as the arbiters when government and parliament exercise their respective powers.

separated-powers.rationale: He describes government and parliament as distinct institutions, each exercising its responsibilities, with voters arbitrating.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He places protection of vulnerable people and inclusion of disabled citizens at the center of public action.

party-commands-army.rationale: Excludes partisan involvement in military affairs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He advocates deeper African integration and coordinated community policies rather than isolated national action.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He explicitly defends equal dignity of cultures and civilizations and rejects any civilization imposing its norms universally.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He proposes separating the presidency from party leadership and leaves his party post, but later revives an electoral coalition; the practical stance is mixed.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His proposed constitutional checks would subject executive action to judicial scrutiny.

common-currency.rationale: He considers a regional currency, a smaller monetary grouping and a national fallback; support depends on feasibility and monetary sovereignty.

patriotic-education.rationale: He calls for training young people in civic discipline and love of the homeland.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: He explicitly recognizes that government must present budget legislation to the National Assembly.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He personally defends the stricter law against same-sex relations against international criticism, beyond merely promulgating it.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Proposes neighborhood assemblies and participatory budgets.

social-market-economy.rationale: He combines support for private business growth with labor regulation, social protection and equitable taxation.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He advocates modernizing and strengthening national armed forces.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: He supports negotiated IMF assistance and fiscal adjustment while insisting on protecting vulnerable households.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He advocates strengthening public police and gendarmerie rather than abolishing them.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He orders an end to foreign military presence, explaining that foreign bases conflict with sovereignty.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He endorses negotiated agreements with representative unions and promises labor reforms reflecting social-partner consensus.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He advocates reforming international financial institutions to address the debt burdens of countries in the Global South.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: He explicitly combines cultural and traditional grounding with scientific, digital and artificial-intelligence skills.

national-resource-control.rationale: He demands African control of resource governance and domestic processing rather than feeding foreign industries alone.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He ties economic sovereignty and national development to decent work, workers’ rights and social justice.

notes: All 490 statements and every remaining null were reviewed. Program references describe proposals rather than enacted measures. Full current speeches and interviews were downloaded and checked across the statement themes. The September 2026 interview establishes personal defense of the same-sex-relations law; this is not inferred from formal presidential assent or Sonko’s views. It also supersedes an assumption that sovereignty entails rejecting IMF negotiations. The constitutional analysis distinguishes presidential proposals, parliamentary initiatives and their contested political setting; departure from formal party office is not treated as proof of complete nonpartisanship. Opposition to foreign bases is not extended to all alliances. Regional free movement is not global open borders. Motherhood-related family-law reforms are not treated as an express position on every aspect of marital authority. Personal polygamy does not establish a legal platform. No living-person inferences.
